us.answer: Yes. Student visa applicants now generally need an in-person interview with a consular officer.

fi.answer: No interview is listed. You apply online, then visit the Finland Application Centre in New Delhi to prove your identity and give fingerprints.

tr.answer: The Turkish Embassy's note lists documents, not an interview. The note dates from 2019, so check with Mosaic Visa, the centre that takes applications in Dhaka.

my.answer: No. EMGS's steps for the student pass do not include an interview.

nz.answer: Possibly. Immigration New Zealand interviews some student visa applicants, and it interviewed Bangladeshi applicants in 2018 to 2020.
nz.practiceNote: These questions are written for the US interview, but the ones about your studies and your money suit any interview.

day.title: Before the day
day.text: Pay the SEVIS fee once your I-20 arrives, at least 3 business days before the interview, and set your social media accounts to public, as the embassy instructs.

day.title: What to bring
day.text: A passport valid for at least six months beyond your stay, the DS-160 confirmation page, the fee receipt and your I-20. Bring your academic records, test scores and proof of how you will pay, in case the officer asks.

day.title: Getting there
day.text: Arrive about 15 minutes before your appointment. Phones, smart watches, laptops, other electronic devices and bags are not allowed, and the embassy has no storage for them.

day.title: After the interview
day.text: Some cases go to administrative processing, which delays the decision, so leave spare time before your flight.

refused.title: A refusal under 214(b)
refused.text: The officer was not satisfied that you qualify, including that you will leave the USA after your studies. It covers that application only: you can apply again with a new form, a new fee and a new interview, and should show what has changed. There is no appeal.

refused.title: A refusal under 221(g)
refused.text: Your application is incomplete or needs administrative processing. You have a year to send what is missing; after that you apply and pay again. It still counts as a refusal.

refused.title: Brokers and fake messages
refused.text: You do not need a visa broker. False information or documents can lead to a refusal and to a ban on later travel to the USA. Real US government messages come from addresses ending in .gov.

practiceIntro: Practice questions written by Pathway around what the officer must decide: that you are a real student, that you can pay, and that you will leave after your studies.

cards.question: Why do you want to study in the USA?
cards.why: The officer checks that study is your real reason for going.
good: Name what your programme offers that you cannot get at home
Keep it about your studies and your plans

cards.question: Why did you choose this university?
cards.why: It shows you chose the place for your studies.
good: Mention something specific, such as a course, a lab or a teacher
Show you know what you will study there

cards.question: What will you study, and why that subject?
cards.why: It shows your plan holds together.
good: Link it to what you have already done
Say it in plain words, not memorised lines

cards.question: Why not study in Bangladesh?
cards.why: The officer checks that study is your real reason for going.
good: Compare what you want to study with what is offered at home
Stay respectful about home

cards.question: Which universities did you apply to, and which admitted you?
cards.why: It shows how you made your choices.
good: Answer simply and truthfully
Know why you chose the one you did

cards.question: What are your test scores and grades?
cards.why: The officer may ask for your academic records and test scores.
good: Know your scores exactly
Bring your score reports and transcripts

cards.question: Tell me about your school.
cards.why: It helps the officer understand your background.
good: Name your school, your group and your results
Keep it short

cards.question: Who will pay for your studies?
cards.why: The officer must see how you will pay.
good: Name each source and roughly how much it covers
Make sure it matches your I-20 and your documents

cards.question: What does your sponsor do, and how much do they earn?
cards.why: The officer must see how you will pay.
good: Know your family's work and income in plain numbers
Bring documents that show them

cards.question: How will you pay for the years after the first?
cards.why: Your proof of funding covers the first year, so the officer may ask about the rest.
good: Explain the plan for every year of the degree
Keep it consistent with your documents

cards.question: Did you receive a scholarship or financial aid?
cards.why: Aid is part of how you will pay.
good: Say how much it is and for how long
Bring the award letter

cards.question: Can you show me your I-20 and financial documents?
cards.why: The officer may ask for proof of how you will pay.
good: Keep your documents in order
Know what each one shows

cards.question: What will you do after you graduate?
cards.why: Under 214(b), the officer must be satisfied that you will leave after your studies.
good: Describe a real plan
A true answer is stronger than a polished one

cards.question: Do you plan to come back to Bangladesh?
cards.why: Under 214(b), the officer weighs the ties that will bring you back.
good: Explain what brings you back, such as family, work or plans
Keep it true and specific

cards.question: What job do you want after this degree?
cards.why: It shows your studies lead somewhere.
good: Name a real job or field
Say where you plan to do it

cards.question: Do you have family in the USA?
cards.why: The officer weighs your ties at home and abroad.
good: Answer truthfully
Never hide a relative: false information can lead to a refusal

cards.question: Where will you live in the USA?
cards.why: It shows you have planned your studies.
good: Say whether you will live on campus or elsewhere
Know the city your university is in

cards.question: How did you hear about this university?
cards.why: It shows how you made your own choice.
good: Say how you found it and what you checked
If an agent helped you, say so honestly
